pypi_hades_2026.description: Shai-Hulud Hades PyPI waves. Wave 1 (2026-06-07): *-setup.pth startup hook -> Bun -> _index.js stealer. Wave 2 (2026-06-08+, OSV campaign 2026-06-compr-woodpecker): split-loader .pth that hunts sys.path for any _index.js, plus trojanized .abi3.so native extensions.

npm_campaigns_h2_2026.description: npm supply-chain campaigns of June-July 2026. Distinct actors reusing the same playbook rather than Shai-Hulud proper: Mastra/easy-day-js (Sapphire Sleet, DPRK), Injective SDK wallet stealer, jscrambler/IronWorm, the aone-cli RAT cluster, and Joyfill/PolinRider. Two of them execute at import time rather than through an install hook, which defeats --ignore-scripts.

mastra_easy_day_js.vector: phishing of a dormant maintainer account; malicious 'easy-day-js' dependency added scope-wide
mastra_easy_day_js.execution: obfuscated postinstall (setup.cjs) -> TLS-bypass fetch of stage 2 -> protocal.cjs RAT

injective_sdk.vector: compromised maintainer identity + repo trusted-publisher (OIDC) auto-publish
injective_sdk.execution: runtime-only: hooks PrivateKey.fromMnemonic/fromHex/generate; NO lifecycle script

jscrambler_ironworm.execution: preinstall hook in 8.14.0-8.17.0; import-time self-executing function in 8.18.0/8.20.0 (defeats --ignore-scripts)

aone_cli_cluster.vector: split loader across a benign-looking dependency tree + private-scope impersonation of @ali/* names
aone_cli_cluster.execution: vm sandbox escape -> staged download -> private Bun runtime at ~/.real/.bin/bun; poisons .skills AI-tool scripts

joyfill_polinrider.family: PolinRider / DEV#POPPER (assessed related to Contagious Interview, DPRK)
joyfill_polinrider.vector: maintainer credential compromise; implant baked into dist bundles at build time
joyfill_polinrider.execution: import-time (not a lifecycle hook); C2 resolved from Tron/Aptos/BSC transactions; worms into the global npm CLI, VS Code, Discord and GitHub Desktop

npm_campaigns_aug_2026.description: August 2026. ChainDrop (2026-08-04) is a Mini Shai-Hulud variant that reached npm through a maintainer's GitHub account rather than through npm itself, so the poisoned tarballs carry genuine GitHub Actions provenance - provenance attests build integrity, not source integrity. Flooding Dropper (2026-08-05) is a different problem entirely: mass dependency-confusion squatting whose dropper fires on require(), not on an install hook.

chaindrop_keyv.actor: Mini Shai-Hulud lineage (worm built on the open-sourced code)
chaindrop_keyv.entry_point: GitHub account takeover of the keyv/cacheable maintainer
chaindrop_keyv.execution: preinstall hook 'node setup.mjs' -> downloaded Bun 1.3.13 -> Math_Symbol.js
chaindrop_keyv.note: Provenance was genuine: the tarballs really were built by that repository, in that workflow, on that commit. Provenance attests build integrity, not source integrity, so signature verification alone would not have caught this.

flooding_dropper.entry_point: dependency confusion - names shadowing internal packages
flooding_dropper.execution: runs on require(), so --ignore-scripts and npm v12 defaults do not help
